Dockerfile packages one service • Docker Compose connects the whole environment

Both services

One Dockerfile, two optimized stages

1

Build stage

Starts from the full .NET SDK.

  • Copies restore metadata first
  • Runs dotnet restore
  • Copies all source
  • Publishes Release output
sdk:10.0
→
2

Runtime stage

Starts from the lean ASP.NET runtime.

  • Copies published output only
  • Runs without build tools
  • Uses container-provided UID
  • Starts the assembly directly
aspnet:10.0

Why it matters: smaller deployment surface and faster restore caching.

src/Services/OrderService/Dockerfile

Build → publish → run

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src

COPY global.json nuget.config Directory.*.props ./
COPY src/Services/OrderService/OrderService.csproj ...
COPY src/Shared/Contracts/Contracts.csproj ...
COPY src/Shared/Messaging/Messaging.csproj ...
COPY src/Shared/ServiceDefaults/ServiceDefaults.csproj ...

RUN dotnet restore src/Services/OrderService/OrderService.csproj
COPY src/ src/
RUN dotnet publish ... -c Release -o /app --no-restore

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app .
USER $APP_UID
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "OrderService.dll"]
01

Dependency-aware restore

Project files are copied before source, allowing Docker to reuse the NuGet cache.

02

One published artifact

dotnet publish produces the executable and dependencies in /app.

03

Minimal runtime

The SDK stage is excluded from the final image.

src/Services/NotificationService/Dockerfile

The same pattern, different entry assembly

OrderService

ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "OrderService.dll"]

Publishes OrderPlaced events through an HTTP API.

NotificationService

ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "NotificationService.dll"]

Runs a background Service Bus subscription processor.

Shared build logic

Both Dockerfiles copy the same shared projects—Contracts, Messaging, and ServiceDefaults—then publish their own application project.

Build, environment & startup

Compose wires source and runtime behavior

↗

Build context

context: .. with the repository root means Dockerfile paths are relative to the project root.

⚙

Environment

Both services receive the emulator connection string and Development environment mode.

1→2

Startup order

depends_on starts dependencies but does not verify readiness.

#

Ports

Only host-facing ports are published. AMQP runs on the shared Docker network.

order-service:
  build:
    context: ..
    dockerfile: src/Services/OrderService/Dockerfile
  ports: ["5085:8080"]
  environment:
    SERVICEBUS__CONNECTIONSTRING: "Endpoint=sb://sb-emulator/;..."
  depends_on: [emulator]
  networks: [sb-emulator]
